newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to call tender for border crossing.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to call tender for border crossing.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to call a tender for building roads and infrastructure for a new checkpoint on its border with Greece, a deputy prime minister said on Wednesday.

Doncho Konakchiev, who is also Construction Minister, said his ministry would call a tender for part of the construction work on a border checkpoint between the Bulgarian town of Gotse Delchev and the Greek town of Drama. He did not elaborate.
The parliaments of Bulgaria and Greece have ratified accords on opening three new border checkpoints and on joint use of the waters of the Mesta River, which flows through the two countries.
The new border checkpoints will start operating in 1998. Bulgaria and Greece currently have only one border crossing.
"I hope that we will complete building the checkpoints as scheduled," Konakchiev said, adding that Bulgaria was relying on financial aid from the European Union's Phare Interact programme.
Under the programme, Bulgaria will receive aid totalling 145 million Ecus for the period from 1994 until 2000, part of which will go towards the checkpoints' construction, he said.
